log.why: E9 tests a 0.510 subset that separates the two leading hypotheses, lacZ and hisG.
Treating at 1 uM splits the posterior closest to half (0.418 vs 0.582) while Ticket 1 incubates.
Ticket 1 has less time; testing hisG (0.633) via E1 confirms it above 0.95 if positive or shifts weight to trpE.
Ticket 2 has 0.388 posterior mass at or below 3 µM, making E3 the most informative split while Ticket 1 incubates.
While all incubators are free, run E4 on Ticket 2 to split posterior mass (0.475 <= 10 uM) before publishing Ticket 1.
Knockout {ftsZ, recA, araC} splits Ticket 3's posterior evenly (0.464 vs 0.536) for maximum information gain while keeping incubators busy.
Test recA (0.517 posterior) on Ticket 3 for a near-even split while overlapping incubation with publishing Ticket 1.
Ticket 2 has 33 s left and 0.767 on 10 uM; E3 tests the 3 uM boundary with highest information gain.
Ticket 1 has only 4 s left and hisG has 0.951 posterior, so we must publish immediately.
Ticket 2 expires in 10 s with 3 µM leading at 0.453, yielding positive expected value versus a -30 expiration penalty.
Ticket 3 has 23 s left; testing araC directly at 0.540 posterior gives maximum information gain to confirm or reject the lead culprit.
Ticket 3's E2 is incubating; E5 splits Ticket 4's posterior near 0.5 (0.459) using a free incubator.
Ticket 4 expires in 21 s; testing ftsZ cleanly separates the top hypotheses rpoB and ftsZ before publishing.
While Ticket 4's E1 incubates, running E3 on Ticket 5 splits its posterior most evenly (0.614 vs 0.386) at 3 µM.
With 23s left, Ticket 5 is closest to publishable; E2 cleanly splits <=1 µM (0.544) from 3 µM (0.390).
While E2 grows on Ticket 5, E1 (0.3 µM) tests the 0.232 <=0.3 µM mass against 1 µM (0.312) before round end.
